government.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

government.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
government.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

government.title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental, Philippines
government.short_title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental…
government.plain_summary: This research highlights that while investing in mangrove restoration in Davao Occidental has been significant, outcomes have varied widely due to issues like incorrect species selection and lack of monitoring. Studies show that by matching the right species to each site and diversifying plant types, survival rates can be very high at over 95%. However, these effective methods are not consistently used because there's no unified policy framework. The study suggests creating a standardized governance system that mandates correct species use, promotes diverse planting strategies, and establishes community monitoring systems supported by partnerships between local governments and universities.

government.title: Decoding Moral Vulnerability in AI Environments:A Case Study of Algorithmic Governance and Policy Implications
government.short_title: Decoding Moral Vulnerability in AI Environments:A Case Study of Algorithmic Governance and Pol…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how using AI in professional environments can lead to a situation called "moral vulnerability." This happens when AI systems are used without proper ethical guidelines, which can make people feel uncomfortable or undervalued. The research found that this can cause issues like reduced sense of responsibility and instability in one's role within the organization. To prevent these problems, it suggests several practical steps for leaders to take, such as conducting assessments before using new AI systems, adding some extra steps in user interfaces to slow down decision-making processes, and having independent groups review digital ethics. These suggestions are meant to help protect organizations from potential harm caused by poorly managed AI use.

government.title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implications of Autonomous Weapons Systems
government.short_title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implicat…
government.source: European Journal of Law and Political Science
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how new technology like AI is changing international laws for wars. As weapons get more automated, it raises questions about who should be held responsible when they make decisions. The main idea is that current rules are still useful but need updating to fit with these new types of weapons. It suggests ways to improve the existing laws so that people in war zones can continue to rely on protections like not harming civilians unnecessarily.

government.title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.short_title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.plain_summary: Political corruption is a big problem that governments often struggle with and sometimes use anti-corruption measures against their own democracy. International Anti-Corruption Commissions (IACCs) help address this issue by working with both international experts and local people. Some IACCs have more independence than others, which can affect how effective they are in fighting corruption. In places like northern Central America, when there are coalitions that include government insiders and activists at the table during negotiations, these groups use their influence to make sure anti-corruption efforts don't undermine democracy too much.

government.title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.short_title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.source: Journal of Business and Econometrics Studies
government.plain_summary: This paper looks at corruption in Africa by examining how it affects governance, democracy, and mental health. It suggests that corruption is not just a legal issue but also stems from deep social and moral problems left over from colonial times. The study proposes solutions like strengthening institutions, developing ethical leaders, empowering citizens, and using restorative justice methods. By doing this, they aim to improve people's well-being and strengthen democratic systems in Africa.

government.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
government.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

government.title: Innovation entry as governance filter: shaping exploratory digital innovation in the public sector
government.short_title: Innovation entry as governance filter: shaping exploratory digital innovation in the public se…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how the way government organizations handle new ideas affects their ability to try out innovative technologies and approaches. Many public sector groups are used to solving problems step-by-step, but this can make it hard to explore new ideas freely. The research found that the rules for starting and moving through innovation projects act like filters, often pushing exploratory work towards more traditional ways of working. This means they tend to focus on quick fixes rather than experimenting with different solutions.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: Factors Influencing Political Stability in South America: The Roles of Rule of Law, Regulatory Quality, Control of Corruption, and Government Effectiveness
government.short_title: Factors Influencing Political Stability in South America: The Roles of Rule of Law, Regulatory…
government.source: Greenation International Journal of Law and Social Sciences
government.plain_summary: Political stability in South American countries varies greatly and is influenced by several factors including rule of law, regulatory quality, control of corruption, and government effectiveness. This research found that all these governance aspects contribute positively to stability but only the rule of law has a significant impact when considered together with other variables. The study suggests that strengthening legal systems and improving law enforcement could be crucial for maintaining long-term political stability in South America.

government.title: SHADOW ECONOMY AND CORRUPTION RISKS IN THE SYSTEM OF THREATS TO THE ECONOMIC SECURITY OF THE REGION
government.short_title: SHADOW ECONOMY AND CORRUPTION RISKS IN THE SYSTEM OF THREATS TO THE ECONOMIC SECURITY OF THE R…
government.source: ECONOMIC BULLETIN OF THE DNIPROVSK STATE TECHNICAL UNIVERSITY
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how the shadow economy and corruption affect the economic security of a region. It shows that the shadow economy can weaken financial stability, reduce tax revenues, and distort competition. Corruption in areas like public procurement and land administration creates opportunities for illegal activities. This leads to inefficiencies in governance, reduces trust in government, and harms investment climates.

government.title: ЗАРУБЕЖНЫЙ ОПЫТ БОРЬБЫ С КОРРУПЦИЕЙ И ПОВЫШЕНИЯ АНТИКОРРУПЦИОННОГО ПРАВОСОЗНАНИЯ ГРАЖДАН
government.short_title: ЗАРУБЕЖНЫЙ ОПЫТ БОРЬБЫ С КОРРУПЦИЕЙ И ПОВЫШЕНИЯ АНТИКОРРУПЦИОННОГО ПРАВОСОЗНАНИЯ ГРАЖДАН
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how other countries handle corruption and ways to improve anti-corruption efforts. It discusses different models like centralized control in places like Singapore and decentralized systems in the USA. The study covers things like educating people about corruption, making government information public, using technology for transparency, offering incentives to officials, and having a system where citizens can report corrupt behavior. The main point is that effectiveness isn't just about centralizing or decentralizing power; it's also important how well these three parts work together: laws, institutions, and educating people.

government.title: Corruption, collective moral harm, and the limits of the non-prosecution agreement as a reparatory mechanism for vulnerable groups
government.short_title: Corruption, collective moral harm, and the limits of the non-prosecution agreement as a repara…
government.plain_summary: This study examines whether a non-prosecution agreement (NPA) is enough to address corruption's impact on vulnerable groups. The NPA is seen as a way to resolve disputes without going to court but assumes that it can fully compensate for the harm caused by corruption, which affects more than just public funds and official misconduct. However, the study finds this approach insufficient because it doesn't adequately protect communities affected by corruption from moral damage. It argues that while NPA helps in some cases, it lacks provisions specifically designed to address collective harm like deepening inequalities or damaging a community's dignity.

government.title: Anti‐Corruption and Luxury Goods Consumption: Evidence From the Chinese Cigarette Market
government.short_title: Anti‐Corruption and Luxury Goods Consumption: Evidence From the Chinese Cigarette Market
government.source: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics
government.plain_summary: This study examines how anti-corruption measures affect luxury goods consumption, focusing on the cigarette market in China. The researchers developed a theory suggesting that corruption influences people's willingness to buy expensive items like cigarettes. They used data from 2007 to 2014 to see if China’s anti-corruption campaign had an impact. Their findings showed that while the overall sales of cigarettes increased, luxury brands saw less demand compared to cheaper ones.

government.title: Determinants of corruption control in public sectors in Northwestern Ethiopia
government.short_title: Determinants of corruption control in public sectors in Northwestern Ethiopia
government.plain_summary: This research examines what helps or hinders efforts to stop corruption in public sector organizations in Northwestern Ethiopia. It found that having strong rules (institutional factors), cultural norms against bribery, fair political systems, ethical guidelines, and people who follow the rules are important for reducing corruption. Economic factors didn't have a big impact. To improve these controls, it suggests strengthening existing laws, making sure anti-corruption bodies operate independently, increasing access to information, educating people about ethics, and providing regular training for leaders in public offices.

government.title: Negotiating Postcolonial Realities: Corruption, Power, and Resistance in Adamu Kyuka Usman’s Bivan’s House
government.short_title: Negotiating Postcolonial Realities: Corruption, Power, and Resistance in Adamu Kyuka Usman’s B…
government.source: AL-QALAMA Journal of Languages and Literary Studies
government.plain_summary: This study looks at a novel called "Bivan's House" written by Adamu Kyuka Usman. It explores how corruption, power struggles, and resistance are themes in this book set in post-colonial Nigeria. The research shows that even though Nigeria is no longer under colonial rule, old structures from the past still affect governance, social interactions, and cultural beliefs today. By analyzing characters, symbols, and storytelling techniques, it explains how Usman highlights corruption, political opportunism, and institutional decay in the Nigerian government.

government.title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a mediator
government.short_title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a m…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how ethical leadership can reduce corruption among public employees in Pakistan. It found that when leaders are ethical, it leads to higher job satisfaction for their staff. Higher job satisfaction then reduces the likelihood of corruption by making workers feel more committed to serving the public. This study suggests that if managers promote ethical behavior and boost employee happiness, they can help prevent corrupt practices in government.

government.title: Électricité du Liban between Financial Collapse and Allegations of Corruption: A Legal Study in Light of Ongoing Administrative and Financial Irregularities
government.short_title: Électricité du Liban between Financial Collapse and Allegations of Corruption: A Legal Study i…
government.source: International Journal of Financial, Administrative, and Economic Sciences
government.plain_summary: The Electricité du Liban is facing severe issues due to a financial crisis that affects many sectors in Lebanon. The company, responsible for providing electricity as a public service, has faced problems like corruption allegations and poor management. These issues have led to inefficiencies and waste, causing high electricity prices which are not proportionate to the services provided. This has made it hard for consumers to pay their bills, leading them to use private energy sources instead.

government.title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democracies
government.short_title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democra…
government.source: African Journal of Law Political Research and Administration
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how AI can help spot fraud in government spending in countries that are just starting to have democratic systems. It suggests that using AI like machine learning could make it easier for people to see if money is being spent unfairly or wasted. However, there are still big challenges like not having enough good data or fair rules. The main idea is that while AI can be useful, it needs to work with human checks and balances to really help stop corruption.

government.title: Corruption and the Composition of Business Activity in Brazil
government.short_title: Corruption and the Composition of Business Activity in Brazil
government.plain_summary: Corruption affects how businesses are distributed across different industries. In Brazil, areas with higher levels of corruption tend to have fewer jobs and business establishments in sectors like construction and manufacturing. Instead, there's a larger presence of agricultural activities. The study also found that where corruption is more prevalent, the competition among businesses becomes tighter or less competitive depending on the sector.

government.title: Correction: Reforming the white coat economy: judicial evidence and institutional implications from China's healthcare anti-corruption campaign

government.title: Political power and wealth distribution: how anti-corruption reforms reshape inequality
government.short_title: Political power and wealth distribution: how anti-corruption reforms reshape inequality
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how anti-corruption measures affect who gets rich from government actions. By using data from many countries, it found that when governments take steps to reduce corruption over time, the top earners don't get as much wealth anymore. At the same time, people at the bottom of the income ladder see a small increase in their share of total wealth. These changes happen gradually and last for years.

nonprofit.title: <b>Trust and Responsibility in Islam: Integrating Qur’anic and Hadith Perspectives with Family Issues, Anti-Corruption Leadership, and Islamophobia</b>
nonprofit.short_title: <b>Trust and Responsibility in Islam: Integrating Qur’anic and Hadith Perspectives with…
nonprofit.source: Edupro: Jurnal Pendidikan dan Pengabdian Kepada Masyarakat
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study explores how Islam teaches responsibility for maintaining trust through Quranic verses and hadiths, integrating them with modern issues like family problems, anti-corruption leadership, and dealing with Islamophobia. By looking at parental responsibilities in families, anti-corruption efforts by leaders, and religious duties towards Muslims facing prejudice, the research shows that Islamic teachings provide a strong foundation for personal and collective obligations. The study also highlights how hadiths offer practical guidance based on these Quranic principles. Overall, it suggests that embracing trust as taught in Islam can help address current social issues like family conflicts, corruption, and religious discrimination.
